title: The 48 Laws of Power
author: Robert Greene
description: The 48 Laws of Power by Robert Greene (Viking/Penguin, 1998), produced with Joost Elffers, an international bestseller on the dynamics of power, influence and manipulation. Greene distils three thousand years of history and the writings of strategists such as Machiavelli, Sun Tzu, Clausewitz, Castiglione and Baltasar Gracián into 48 laws, such as 'Never outshine the master', 'Conceal your intentions', 'Always say less than necessary', 'Court attention at all costs' and 'Crush your enemy totally'. Each law is illustrated with historical anecdotes of its observance and its transgression, interpretation, and 'reversal' cases where it should not be applied, with marginal quotations and fables. Amoral by design, the book is widely read in business, politics and popular culture. It sits in the library's Other section as a classic of strategic and psychological realism rather than spirituality.
